subject: Post-demo recap & infra asks: private peering + tool-calls
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@nimbus.ai>, rohit.sen@nimbus.ai
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & infra asks: private peering + tool-calls

Hi Aaron / Rohit —

Thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and the infra/tech asks we discussed so we can scope a short pilot: 

1) Objective: Pilot Redwood inference for semantic search + a lightweight reranker over your customer support corpus. We demonstrated the embeddings flow + a toy reranker. Goal is a sandbox PoC with real data and a follow-up load test.

2) Networking ask (needed for PoC planning):
   - Do you prefer inbound connectivity (AWS PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint Service) or outbound-only (Redwood egress to your IP allowlist / static NAT)?
   - If PrivateLink, who owns the endpoint service? If outbound, can you provide the static egress ranges / proxy egress pattern?
   - TLS/mTLS expectations: do you require mutual TLS for API calls, and do you have a cert rotation cadence we should align with?

3) Auth & SDKs:
   - We support short-lived API credentials (rotating API keys / OAuth service account tokens). For the PoC, a long-lived API key scoped to the sandbox is fine; for production we recommend short TTL + automatic rotation via your secret manager.

4) Structured outputs & tool-calling:
   - We suggested using our tool-calling schema to return an actionable rerank request (json schema we can share). Please confirm any required fields (id, query, top_k, context_source) so we can prototype end-to-end.

5) Embeddings & reranker options:
   - Option A: Redwood hosts embeddings and the lightweight reranker; you call the reranker via our tool-call API.
   - Option B: We provide embeddings only; you run the reranker inside your VPC with a small model to avoid egress for full-text scoring.

Attached: placeholder network diagram you mentioned (nimbus-network-diagram.png).

Next steps: if you can share network constraints and preferred connectivity model by EOD Monday (4/5), Sergio will draft two PoC architectures and Marcus will prepare the sample tool-calling schema. We can set a 60-min architecture workshop after that.

- Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@nimbus.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohit Sen <rohit.sen@nimbus.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & infra asks: private peering + tool-calls

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side (high level) and attaching our internal network diagram with egress notes.

- Preference: outbound-only preferred. Our security team is conservative about accepting inbound endpoint services.
- Environment: AWS-heavy (us-east-1 primary). We currently egress through a corporate HTTP proxy that NATs through a small set of static IPs used for allowlisting. We can expose those ranges to Redwood.
- mTLS: Preferred for server-to-server calls. We can accept mTLS to a customer-managed load balancer (ALB/NLB) but prefer Redwood authenticate to us (client cert) rather than Redwood terminating mTLS on your side.
- Auth: Short-lived OAuth tokens preferred, but for the PoC a scoped API key is acceptable.
- Reranker: We are leaning to Option B (embeddings hosted; reranker in-VPC) to keep scoring local for privacy/perf. We still want a demo of hosted reranker so we can compare latency/cost.

Technical contacts who should be in the PoC workshop:
- Rohit Sen, Senior Engineer, Infrastructure (rohit.sen@nimbus.ai)
- Priya Menon, Security Architect (priya.menon@nimbus.ai) — copying Priya on separate mail with questionnaire.

We attached our network diagram and the list of static egress IP ranges (nimbus-network-diagram.png). Will aim to get the security questionnaire back early next week.

Thanks,
Aaron
Director of Engineering, Nimbus Analytics
aaron.cho@nimbus.ai

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@nimbus.ai>, Rohit Sen <rohit.sen@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & infra asks: private peering + tool-calls

Hi Aaron / Rohit —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Based on outbound-only + mTLS-to-customer-preference, I sketched two concrete PoC options below (attached as rdw-arch-options.pdf). High-level tradeoffs included.

PoC Option 1 — Outbound egress to static IPs (recommended short path for PoC):
  - Redwood egresses to your allowlisted static IPs / corporate proxy.
  - Mutual TLS terminated at your NLB/ALB. Redwood will present client certs.
  - Auth: scoped API key for PoC; migrate to short-lived OAuth client credentials for production.
  - Pros: minimal infra changes on your side; fastest to stand up.
  - Cons: cert management & rotation coordination; egress path still crosses your proxy (adds latency).

PoC Option 2 — AWS PrivateLink (longer lead):
  - We expose a PrivateLink endpoint service in our account; you create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC.
  - mTLS still supported but PrivateLink keeps traffic on the AWS network (no public egress).
  - Pros: better isolation, simpler IP management, consistent latency.
  - Cons: requires inbound endpoint acceptance and network ops time.

Other items:
  - Service accounts / credential rotation: we can integrate with your KMS/secrets manager to fetch ephemeral creds (recommended for production). For PoC we will issue a time-boxed API key and support rotating it mid-PoC.
  - Structured tool-calling / rerank schema: attached sample-tool-schema.json. Key fields we suggest: {"request_id","query","top_k","candidate_ids","context_refs","model_hint","priority"}. We can add any Nimbus-specific fields (customer_id, segment) as needed.
  - Embeddings pipeline: two patterns 
     a) Push embeddings to your S3 bucket via presigned upload (no inbound connection to you).
     b) Host embeddings on Redwood and expose a read-only retrieval API over TLS (requires allowlist).

Action items I can own this week: draft a PoC runbook for Option 1 (egress -> static IPs + mTLS) and sample cURL snippets for mTLS+API-key auth. Marcus will prepare a short demo showing hosted reranker latency vs local reranker (cost delta and rough token estimates).

Attachments: rdw-arch-options.pdf, sample-tool-schema.json

Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Thanks — excited to get this moving.
